messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a SCIM deprovision loop for a handful of accounts after yesterday's RBAC cleanup. Looks related to SAML assertion audience mismatch and KMS decrypt errors in the provisioner logs. Can someone help triage?

devon: ok — can you paste the provisioner log lines and one failing SAML assertion (sanitized)?

maria.chen: pasting logs + assertion (sanitized) below:
```
2026-02-18T14:12:03Z provisioner ERROR user-sync failed uid=joe@example.com error=KMSDecryptError key=alias/service-scim region=us-west-2
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z provisioner WARN deprovision queued uid=joe@example.com reason=identity_mismatch
2026-02-18T14:12:05Z scim HTTP 200 -> PATCH /Users/joe@example.com payload={"active":false}
```
SAML assertion (sanitized):
```
<Assertion>
  <Subject>joe@example.com</Subject>
  <Audience>https://redwood-infer.example.com/auth/saml</Audience>
  <Attribute Name=\"externalId\">joe@example.com</Attribute>
</Assertion>
```

ashley.c: quick q — the RBAC cleanup changed group names (prod-eng -> infra-eng) and we rotated a KMS alias for the service account yesterday afternoon. Might be related.

samir: sounds like two concurrent failure modes: 1) KMS alias rotation -> provisioner can't decrypt encrypted externalId -> attribute blank -> deprovision decision; 2) Audience in SAML doesn't match our SP after recent hostname change -> identity mismatch. Both could trigger deprovision loop.

maria.chen: how do we confirm the KMS decrypt path is hitting the right alias? logs show alias/service-scim but the rotation created alias/service-scim-v2. Is that expected?

devon: run `aws kms list-aliases --key-id <keyid>` and check alias/targetKeyId mapping from the instance role that runs the provisioner. Also check that the provisioner environment variable KMS_ALIAS still points to `alias/service-scim` (not -v2). If alias was re-pointed to new key but the old alias deleted, calls will fail.

samir: another quick check: in the provisioner pod, do `env | grep KMS` and `curl -s -H \"X-Forwarded-Host: redwood-infer.example.com\" https://internal-sp/metadata` to confirm SP EntityID/audience. If Audience != Assertion Audience we saw, that confirms mismatch.

opsec-bot: [ALERT] 2026-02-18T14:15:00Z — Detected repeated deprovision events for 7 users in production; created incident INC-2026-1423.

ashley.c: filing as P1? these are user-facing deprovs. I'm pausing the automated RBAC prune job in k8s cronjob `rbac-cleanup-prod` (disabled) — will update when done.

maria.chen: thanks. I'm going to: 1) verify KMS alias mapping, 2) re-run one sync in dry-run mode with verbose logging to ensure externalId decrypt output, 3) compare SP EntityID. Will post results in ~15m.

devon: if KMS alias rotated and we need immediate fix, easiest rollback is to re-create alias/service-scim pointing to previous key (if still available) or update provisioner env var to the new alias and restart deployment. Prefer less blast radius: prefer env var update + restart on a single canary pod first.

samir: also add a guard in provisioner: if externalId decryption fails, log warning and skip deprov decision for 24h window (so we avoid automated churn during infra ops). Could be a config flag.

maria.chen: agreed. I'll add a ticket for a short-term guard and keep the immediate triage focused on KMS alias + audience mismatch. Posting findings in 12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria.chen: update — KMS alias was re-pointed but old alias deleted. We recreated alias/service-scim -> previousKeyId and the provisioner decrypts succeed for a sample user. SP EntityID also needed a small host rewrite (we had an nginx hostname rewrite that changed the Audience). Fixing nginx rewrite now and will run a full dry-run sync.

devon: awesome. After dry-run, watch the incident INC-2026-1423 and let's hold auto-deprovision for 1h. Also open a postmortem to cover alias rotation SOP + provisioner resilience.

ashley.c: RBAC job still paused. I'll unpause after we confirm no churn in the next 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
summary: SCIM deprovision loop after RBAC change traced to KMS alias rotation + SAML Audience mismatch; temporary mitigations and follow-ups planned
